artifact_schema.description: The discrete logarithm, as 33 lowercase hex characters.

k.description: k with [k]P = Q, in [1, n), zero-padded to exactly 33 lowercase hex characters.

statement: Solve Certicom's ECC2K-130, open since 1997: find k with [k]P = Q on the Koblitz curve y^2 + xy = x^3 + 1 over GF(2^131) pinned in the checker. The parameters are the challenge's own and are authenticated by arithmetic rather than by their source -- the reduction polynomial irreducible, #E = 4n by the Frobenius recursion, n prime, P and Q on the curve and of order n -- so a corrupted digit could not have survived. THIS IS A FRONTIER OBJECTIVE AND IS NOT EXPECTED TO SETTLE. Pollard rho with the <-1> x <sigma> speed-up needs about 2^60.81 group operations, about 40000 GPU-hours at the 14.1e9 iterations/s one 2026 GPU measures. It is posted because the network should carry an externally-defined benchmark whose difficulty nobody here chose. Certicom's own prize is NOT claimable: BlackBerry retired the challenge and the pages are gone; this objective pays cairn's reward and nothing of Certicom's. The search itself is paid by objective-ecc2k130-orbit-batch.json, orbit by orbit, and that is the objective a contributor works. Submit {"k"} as 33 lowercase hex characters, k in [1, n). See examples/certicom-ecdlp/README.md and docs/design/orbit-piecework.md.
